text:
Here are the strongest open-ear options for running, based on the reviews and listings I found.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds.** This is a clip-on design with physical buttons, which WIRED and Runner's World both find easier than touch controls while running. Sound is clearer than most competitors'. The trade-offs are a 7-hour battery and IPX4 water resistance. Runner's World lists them at $199 on sale (down from $299). Reviews: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) and [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/).

- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.** Sound travels through your cheekbones and a bass-producing air-conduction driver, so your ears stay fully open. WIRED calls the bass a big improvement and gives it 8/10, though clarity is a step back from the older model. It has a 12-hour battery, IP55 rating, and USB-C charging. Runner's World lists it at $180 (WIRED notes it's often $125 at retailers like REI and Best Buy). Reviews: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) and [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946). RTINGS found the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is more durable and has multi-device pairing.

- **Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2.** Its 10-hour battery (40 hours with the case) and IP57 rating stand out. It's $200 per WIRED and Runner's World. Source: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/).

- **Best value hook-style: Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It has a 10-hour battery (42 with the case), IP55 rating, and LDAC for Android users. Prices vary by source. Dealectric lists $129.99 at Soundcore's US store, while SoundGuys lists $99.99 MSRP and $79.99 at Amazon. A code, AFSC20, was reported working on 2026-10-22 for $25.99 off full-price items (not sale items), and it expires 2026-12-31. The store's checkout has the final word on the code. [Buy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) (affiliate link: Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you). Sources: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2) and [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/).

- **Best budget: JLab Flex Open (Flex Ear Clips).** It costs about $40 to $50 and is a low-risk way to test whether clip-ons work for you. Sound is less detailed than pricier pairs, and it has touch controls only. Source: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/).

- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys names it its best pick for running. It's listed at $99 on Amazon (MSRP $149) with IP54 rating and good bass for an open design. Source: [SoundGuys workout earbuds](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/).

**How to choose**

- If traffic awareness matters most, choose bone conduction (OpenRun Pro 2) or a clip-on with better sound (Bose).
- If you want the best value, try the AeroFit 2 or the JLab Flex.
- If you run in the rain or want longer battery life, look at the OpenDots 2.

**Caveats**

- Open-ear designs leak sound and provide no isolation, so other people can hear your music at higher volumes.
- These don't guarantee safety. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic and people around you.
- Prices change often. Confirm the price at checkout.
- I couldn't find direct buy links for the Bose, Shokz, or JLab models in these results, so the links above go to the reviews. Search the retailers listed in those reviews to buy.
